text:
Anya Petrov: Follow-up RFC thread: KMS-escrow and offline upgrade handshake. High-level goal: allow customer operators to rotate signing keys locally and provide a recoverable wrapped-key escrow without exfiltrating raw private key material.
Matt Cheng: Suggest we support two modes:
- operator-managed HSM (customer controls key, Redwood stores wrapped blob)
- provider-assisted threshold escrow (split shares between customer and Redwood KMS)
Julie Park: Threat model note: attacker with access to both Redwood and operator consoles could still reconstruct unless we require hardware-backed attestation and operator approval. Recommend adding time-lock and multi-approval policy for release.
Samir Patel: Air-gapped UX:
1) On build host, CI creates release manifest + `release-seal` (sha256 manifest + metadata).
2) Operator pulls `release-installer` onto an offline admin machine.
3) On offline machine, operator uses hardware token to sign `release-seal` and generate `wrap-key` that encrypts the signing key. Produces `escrow.json` and a short human-readable `recovery-instructions.txt` with stepwise ops guidance.
Julie Park: Minimal `escrow.json` fields we should require: `version`, `wrapped_key_b64`, `wrap_alg`, `signer_pub`, `expiry_iso`, `nonce`, `origin_manifest_sha256`, `attestation_statement_b64`.
Sample:
```
{
  "version":"1",
  "wrapped_key_b64":"...",
  "wrap_alg":"RSA-OAEP-256",
  "signer_pub":"-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----",
  "expiry_iso":"2026-08-01T00:00:00Z",
  "nonce":"r3l3as3-01",
  "origin_manifest_sha256":"c0ffee...",
  "attestation_statement_b64":"MIIBIj..."
}
```
ops-bot: escrow-schema v1 validated.
Matt Cheng: API for redwood-agent: POST /v1/escrow -> validates attestation, origin manifest, expiry, and stores blob metadata. GET /v1/escrow/:id -> returns metadata but not raw wrapped key unless requester has a hardware-backed session and multi-approval token.
Julie Park: Recovery flow should require a threshold of approvals: operator + security officer + Redwood on-call. Each approval produces a release token that is time-bound and recorded in audit logs.
Samir Patel: Operational edgecases: hardware token lost -> operator can reconstruct via shard recovery (Shamir) but only if they present two-of-three shards with auditor present. Documented in recovery-instructions.txt.
Anya Petrov: Action items: I'll draft RFC section with sequence diagram, attestation contract, minimal escrow schema, and proposed agent API. Also include sample `recovery-instructions.txt` template. Posting draft tomorrow morning. Thanks all!
